body:
Looking back at the curiosity work, this is probably where the capstone became more personally mine without me actively trying to make it about the capstone.

The AI friend question is interesting. NPCs are interesting. Games and immersion are things I genuinely want to work on eventually. Making a computer is something I still want to know how to do. That does not mean they belong here. What actually stayed was more like: what makes people unique if so much behaviour can be learned, why do we voluntarily give useful systems more control, what happens to authorship when the difficult part can be skipped, and what is happening between thought and expression before something becomes finished.

That last one keeps becoming more important to me.

I think faster than I explain sometimes. There is a gap between the thought and the version another person receives. You have something in your head, then language already changes it, then trying to make it understandable changes it again, and then another person interprets it through themselves anyway. AI enters exactly in that gap and basically says, give it to me, I can make this clearer.

And sometimes it actually does. That is the annoying part. I can give something messy and get something back that is structured, concise and technically easier for somebody else to understand, but then I read it and think yea, that is what I meant, but I would never say it like that. So did it help express me or did it turn what I meant into something more acceptable and readable? I did not properly have that distinction in the first presentation.

I also think the perfection thing belongs in the project more than I initially realised. If you are constantly trying to improve something, cleaner sentence, cleaner design, fewer mistakes, more understandable idea, AI fits really easily into that because it can constantly suggest something “better”. But better according to what? Cleaner? Faster? More conventional? More readable? More like other things that already worked? And if all the weird turns in thinking get cleaned before they reach anything, maybe the inefficient part was actually the thing that could have become different. I think that uncertainty is useful.

What is weak about the curiosity assignment is that it is still a dump. I can connect almost anything back to AI or identity if I sit with it long enough because my interests overlap. That does not mean I should. I need to separate “I can connect this” from “this actually needs to be in the project”.

The line I would keep from this point is: I want to understand how to use something that makes me more capable without letting its idea of better slowly become my own.
